# POGS model-substitution study - comparison

*Generated by `compare.py` from each row's artefacts. Do not edit by hand; regenerate with `python shared/compare.py`.*

> **Scope.** Every row is measured against row 00 on the same synthetic data. The POGS authors released no trained POGS checkpoint and no capture scene, so there is no published baseline and no row here claims to beat POGS as published.

## Rows

| row | detection | features | alignment | open-vocab | masks | POGS | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `00_baseline_detic_dinov2_clip` | `detic` | `dino_vits14` | `clip_vitb16` | yes | yes | **stock** | not run |
| `01_locateanything_dinotxt` | `locateanything3d` | `dino_txt` | `dino_txt` | yes | **no** | patched | measured |
| `02_rfdetr_dinov3_mobileclip` | `rfdetr` | `dinov3` | `mobileclipv2` | **no** | yes | patched | measured (dinov3 gated) |
| `03_vfmdetr_siglip2` | `detic` | `dino_vits14` | `siglip2` | yes | yes | patched | not run |
| `04_yolo` | `yolo` | `dino_vits14` | `clip_vitb16` | **no** | **no** | **stock** | not run |

`stock` means the row runs an unmodified POGS tree, which is what makes row 00 the reference. `patched` means stock POGS hardcoded the models it uses and the substitution had to be expressed as a patch; each row's `RESULTS.md` section 6 carries the diff.

## Latency - deterministic

| row | scene | input | roles measured | total fp16 (ms) | vs baseline | per-model fp16 (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `01_locateanything_dinotxt` | `pendulum_v2_30` | 640x480 | **1/3** | 170.82 | - | dino_txt 170.8 |
| `02_rfdetr_dinov3_mobileclip` | `pickplace_v2` | 1280x720 | **1/3** | 48.70 | - | rfdetr 48.7 |

**A bold `roles measured` means the row's `total` is not a pipeline total.** Models that failed to load are absent from the sum, so a row missing its feature model looks cheap rather than unmeasured. The missing ones are listed under *Blocked models* below.

**`00_baseline_detic_dinov2_clip` was not benchmarked on this scene set**, so there is nothing to ratio against and `vs baseline` is empty for every row. Its figures are in `RESULTS.md`, measured on `pickplace` at the same 1280x720.

**These rows were not all benchmarked on the same input size** (1280x720, 640x480), because a row is benchmarked on the scenes it was run on. Latency scales with input, so compare the per-model figures within one `input` value and not down the `total` column; `vs baseline` is left blank where the sizes differ.

## Tracking error per scene - stochastic

Centroid error in mm, lower is better. **-** means that row has not been tracked on that scene yet. **`lost@N`** means the tracker lost the object at frame N, so that cell is not a measurement - see below.

| row | `pendulum_v2_05` | `pendulum_v2_10` | `pendulum_v2_15` | `pendulum_v2_20` | `pendulum_v2_25` | `pendulum_v2_30` | `pendulum_v2_40` | `pendulum_v2_50` | `pendulum_v2_60` | `pickplace_v2` | scenes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `00_baseline_detic_dinov2_clip` | 446.5 | 37.1 | 339.0 | 158.1 | 67.8 | 141.1 | 359.7 | 172.1 | 101.1 | 280.9 | 10/10 |
| `01_locateanything_dinotxt` | 488.2 | 98.7 | 32.6 | 204.5 | 329.0 | 473.8 | 202.3 | 283.6 | 248.2 | 146.7 | 10/10 |
| `02_rfdetr_dinov3_mobileclip` | 208.8 | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | 1/10 |
| `03_vfmdetr_siglip2` | 37.5 | 243.5 | 428.4 | 115.9 | 358.0 | 77.5 | 102.1 | 401.3 | 209.3 | 47.4 | 10/10 |
| `04_yolo` | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | 0/10 |

Centroid error is **displacement error against the generator's ground truth**, `|(est_i - est_0) - (gt_i - gt_0)|`, per tracked part, averaged only over frames where the object actually moved. Lower is better. Every row must use the same `opt_iters` (15, as in stock POGS demos) for the comparison to mean anything.

The pendulum columns are a difficulty ladder: the cylinder's peak displacement grows with the angle, so a row that holds up at 60 degrees is doing something a row that only holds at 5 is not. `pickplace` is the occlusion case, a different kind of difficulty rather than a bigger one.

**A `lost@N` cell cannot be compared with one that held, in either direction.** The tracker goes on scoring after it loses the object, so the figure is the drift of an estimate that is no longer following anything. Lost late, that inflates the error; lost early, it *deflates* it, because an estimate frozen near frame 0 scores the same as assuming the object never moved - and on a small-amplitude scene that is the lowest number the column can produce. Read those cells as failures whatever their value, and do not rank on them.

## Blocked models

- `01_locateanything_dinotxt`: `locateanything3d`
- `02_rfdetr_dinov3_mobileclip`: `rfdetr (fp32)`, `dinov3`, `mobileclipv2`

## Reading this table

- **Latency and detector IoU are deterministic.** They involve no training, so they carry no seed variance and small differences are real.
- **Centroid error and PSNR are stochastic.** POGS seeds nothing of its own - `dino_feats` init, `random_quat_tensor`, the datamanager's `randperm` calls and HDBSCAN clustering are all unseeded - so these are one sample at `machine.seed = 42`.
- **A model that is not open-vocabulary cannot serve POGS**, however fast it is. POGS passes a `custom_vocab` to its detector and consumes per-instance masks.
